title: Mermaids: Not a real thing
summary: Josh and Chuck explore mermaid lore, history and mythology, noting there is no evidence mermaids exist. They cover the Israeli town of Kiryat Yam's standing offer for mermaid proof, the ancient Babylonian sea god Ea, Pliny's neriad, Hans Christian Andersen's darker Little Mermaid ending, Atargatis of Syria, West African Mami Wata, German nixes, and the duality of mermaid myths. They discuss 'eyewitness' accounts including Columbus's manatee sighting, John Smith, the 1830 Scottish Benbecula mermaid, and a 1400s Dutch story. They cover Carl Bantas's tongue-in-cheek 1982-style paper on the extinct mermaid species, the Discovery Channel mockumentary and its sequel, and the professional mermaid shows in Weeki Wachee, Florida. Closing segment asks listeners for iTunes reviews and jingles.

entities.name: Mermaids: The Biology, Their Biology, Culture and Demise

segments.title: Opening banter: Splash, rock stars, and time-machine jokes
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with chat about the movie Splash, Neil Young, the Police reunion, and the Ramones, then joke about faking mermaid photos for profit in the 1920s. They tease the topic and move toward mermaid lore.

segments.title: Kiryat Yam mermaid offer and the 2009 photo
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Israeli coastal town of Kiryat Yam, which offers one million dollars for proof of the mermaid said to live there, a tourism ploy inspired partly by Loch Ness. A distant 2009 photo of a mermaid on a rock surfaced.

segments.title: Mermaid mythology and misogyny in folklore
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck discuss mythology's appeal and how many folk tales were versions of one another with simple moral lessons, often rooted in misogyny. They mention Pliny the Elder's neriad and the Babylonian sea god Ea, a possible predecessor of Poseidon and Neptune.

segments.title: Hans Christian Andersen's original Little Mermaid
segments.summary: The hosts summarize the darker original Little Mermaid story, in which she fails to kill the prince with a knife from her sisters, dissolves into sea foam, and may become an air spirit able to earn heaven by helping humans. They also mention ancient tales of merman boarding ships and sinking them.

segments.title: Mermaids as sirens and luring sailors; Atargatis
segments.summary: The hosts describe mermaid appearance and how mermaids lure sailors through beauty, distinguishing them from sirens, who are bird-women. They then recount the Syrian goddess Atargatis, who killed her human lover by accident and became a fish-tailed mermaid after failing to fully transform.

segments.title: Mami Wata, German nixes, and mythological hybrids
segments.summary: The hosts discuss river-dwelling German nixes that drowned men, and West African Mami Wata, a nurturing water mother who turns murderous if crossed. They note that many mythical hybrids such as centaurs and minotaurs exist, and suggest some scholars link them to a relaxed attitude toward bestiality.

segments.title: Eyewitness accounts: Columbus, John Smith, Benbecula, and Adam
segments.summary: The hosts go through purported sightings. Columbus wrote of three mermaids in his diary, likely manatees. John Smith said he fell in love with a sea creature with long green hair. A 1830 Benbecula town in Scotland reportedly killed and buried a mermaid, and a 1400s Dutch story told of a mute mermaid raised as a girl. Explanations include suggestibility and mistaken identity.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: A short break in the episode is taken, with the hosts joking about neck rubs.

segments.title: Carl Bantas's paper on the extinct mermaid
segments.summary: Chuck describes Carl Bantas's tongue-in-cheek but straight-faced paper in the journal Limnology and Oceanography about an extinct mermaid species, covering its warm-water habitat, diet, and horny skinfolds. Bantas argued that jellyfish stings from ecological imbalance caused their extinction.

segments.title: Discovery Channel mermaid mockumentary
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Discovery Channel mockumentary that aired as if real, its sequel driven by ratings, the NOAA statement that no evidence of mermaids exists, and Torsten Schmidt, the fictional marine geologist, later spotted as an actor resembling Zach Galifianakis.

segments.title: Weeki Wachee professional mermaids
segments.summary: The hosts describe professional mermaid performance, including the Weeki Wachee shows in Florida that drew Elvis Presley and Don Knotts, the training needed for the mermaid crawl and breath-holding, and performers who act as ecology advocates.

segments.title: Listener requests and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts ask listeners to leave iTunes reviews, tell friends, and send jingles, then sign off with website and social media information.
